html:
A law issued on 27 February 380 by Theodosius I, with his co-emperors, which made Nicene Christianity the religion of the Roman Empire.

It told all peoples under Roman rule to follow the faith of the bishops of Rome and Alexandria: one God in three equal persons. Anyone else was a heretic, to be punished by God and by the state. The main target was Arianism, which held that the Son was below the Father and had been favoured by the emperor Valens.

Seventy years earlier Christians had been hunted in the Great Persecution. Now the state defined true belief by law. A year later the First Council of Constantinople settled the creed, and in the 390s pagan sacrifice was banned. The edict was later copied into the Theodosian Code.
sum: A law issued on 27 February 380 by Theodosius I, with his co-emperors, which made Nicene Christianity the religion of the Roman Empire.
